subject: Pricing anchor & GPU lane sizing — post-demo clarifications
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Mark Jensen <mark.jensen@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing anchor & GPU lane sizing — post-demo clarifications

Mark — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick post-call recap + clarifying asks so we can put a procurement-ready proposal on your desk. High-level notes from the call: 

- Expected steady-state tokens: ~200M tokens/month (initial pilot)
- Upside / eventual target: 1B+ tokens/month if model fidelity and latency hold
- Target unit economics you called out: roughly $18–$25 / 1M tokens as a goal range
- Preferred hardware: you said you "prefer H100-equivalent runs for latency", but open to A100-equivalent if it meaningfully improves unit cost
- Throughput/latency SLO: p95 latency target ~300ms for ~512-token responses; concurrency profile: bursts to ~80 concurrent requests

As next steps I promised:
1) Two committed-reserved SKU anchors (H100-equivalent and A100-equivalent) with examples of unit economics at a few monthly token volumes
2) Bench numbers we ran in the demo harness (attached benchmark-results-20270315.csv) and the short note on assumptions (batching, avg response length 512 tokens, typical prompt prefix caching)
3) A procurement-friendly SOW template and pricing slide for your procurement team to review

Quick ask for you: can you confirm whether the $40k–$60k/month budget window you mentioned is a strict cap for Q2 or a target range we should try to beat? Also paste the procurement contact (if not procurement@nimblehealth.com) so we can include them on the SOW.

Attaching a draft proposal template (nimble_proposal_template_v1.pdf) and the raw bench csv. I put Marissa and Dylan on copy — Marissa will own SOW language, Dylan will own ops/throughput assumptions.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0183

From: Mark Jensen <mark.jensen@nimblehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: NimbleHealth Procurement <procurement@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing anchor & GPU lane sizing — post-demo clarifications

Jordan — thanks for the recap and the attachments. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Budget: we have a procurement window for Q2 with an approval band of $40k–$60k/month. That is what we can commit to this quarter; if the numbers look strong and latency holds, we can expand mid-year.
- Unit economics target: our internal goal is ~$20 / 1M tokens — that's what procurement will use for ROI calculations.
- Hardware / lanes: we are leaning toward the H100 path for the initial reserved lanes because of latency. From our side we'd be comfortable evaluating a 6-lane H100-equivalent reservation as the right balance between headroom and cost.
- Success criteria: p95 latency for 512-token responses under normal traffic <= 300ms; stable KV cache behavior (no cache thrash during peak); automated fallback to a slightly cheaper model if capacity issues occur.

Procurement contact is procurement@nimblehealth.com — they asked that any SOW be explicit about data residency (US only) and audit logs retention (90 days). Also please include a straightforward cancellation and ramp schedule in the SOW (we prefer 60-day ramp windows for scaling up or down).

If you can send the two SKU anchors with monthly commitment numbers and a simple per-1M token calculation for a few volume tiers (200M / 1B / 1.5B), procurement will review.

— Mark
Mark Jensen
Head of Platform
NimbleHealth
mark.jensen@nimblehealth.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Mark Jensen <mark.jensen@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing anchor & GPU lane sizing — post-demo clarifications

Mark — appreciate the clarity. Below are two anchors (A and B) that reflect committed-reserved pricing + the implied $/1M tokens at three consumption tiers. I included the assumptions at the bottom. Please let me know which one to turn into a procurement SOW (we can produce a standard 6/12/24 month term template).

PROPOSAL ANCHORS (committed, monthly billing):

Option A — H100-equivalent reserved lanes (recommended for latency-sensitive workloads)
- Reserved: 6 H100-equivalent lanes
- Monthly commitment: $35,000 / month
- Implied $ / 1M tokens (by monthly consumption):
  • 200M tokens/mo => $35,000 / 200 = $175 / 1M tokens
  • 1,000M (1B) tokens/mo => $35,000 / 1000 = $35 / 1M tokens
  • 1,750M (1.75B) tokens/mo => $35,000 / 1750 = $20 / 1M tokens

Option B — A100-equivalent reserved lanes (cost-first, slightly higher latency tradeoff)
- Reserved: 8 A100-equivalent lanes
- Monthly commitment: $28,000 / month
- Implied $ / 1M tokens (by monthly consumption):
  • 200M tokens/mo => $28,000 / 200 = $140 / 1M tokens
  • 1,000M tokens/mo => $28,000 / 1000 = $28 / 1M tokens
  • 1,400M (1.4B) tokens/mo => $28,000 / 1400 = $20 / 1M tokens

Notes and how to read these anchors:
- The per-1M numbers are purely arithmetic: monthly commitment divided by total million tokens consumed. They are meant to show how unit economics improve as utilization scales; our recommended path is to start at a smaller pilot (H100 6-lane) and agree on clear ramp milestones so you hit the mid-/high-tier economics fast.
- Throughput/latency assumptions: these anchors assume the benchmark profile we ran in the demo: 512-token avg responses, caching on prompt prefixes (30% cache hit), continuous batching tuned to p95 latency <= 300ms. If your real workload uses shorter responses or higher cache hit rates, effective $/1M will improve.
- Commitment terms: these prices assume a 12-month committed plan with a standard 60-day scaling window. Shorter terms (3–6 months) increase monthly price ~15–25%.
- Extra add-ons: 24/7 SRE on-call, dedicated routing, and extended observability are add-on line items (we can show those on the SOW but they are optional for the pilot).

Attachments: I updated proposed-sku-comparison.xlsx (attached) with line-item math and a one-page SOW snapshot. Also pointing procurement to the HubSpot deal (link below) so we can attach the SOW there.

If those anchors look in-range, Marissa will prepare the SOW and a plain-language ramp chart showing how you get from 200M -> 1.75B and the expected time to hit $20 / 1M.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
(Attachment: proposed-sku-comparison.xlsx; benchmark-results-20270315.csv)

Assumptions used for calculations: average response length 512 tokens; 30% prefix cache hit; sustained concurrency target 60–80 concurrent requests during peak; batching tuned for p95 <= 300ms.

Jordan — I saw Mark's note and your anchors. I'll take the lead on turning Option A into a procurement SOW. Action items for me: 

- Draft SOW with 12-month term, 60-day scale windows, US-only data residency, 90-day audit logs retention.
- Add explicit acceptance criteria: p95 latency <= 300ms for 512 tokens, KV cache stability, fallback policy to A100-equivalent variant.
- Attach the benchmark CSV and the proposed SKU comparison.
- Share SOW with Mark + procurement@nimblehealth.com by EOD tomorrow for initial procurement review.

Dylan — can you validate the latency/caching language and confirm we can run a short 24-hr soak test on 6 H100-equivalent lanes to generate the 1-week extrapolated numbers? If yes, I'll include a "soak test" line in the SOW as a pre-procurement acceptance step.

I'll follow up with a SOW PDF and a one-slide pricing summary.

— Marissa
